title: What to watch at the open
text: Stocks are about to open after a strong Tuesday. The S&P 500 fund SPY ended at $769.66, up 0.6%, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ ended at $721.25, up 1.3%. The big event today is the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at 2:00 PM Eastern time, so the morning may be calm and the afternoon bumpy. Watch chip stocks, which jumped yesterday, to see if they hold their gains. This is for learning, not advice.

title: The Fed decides today at 2:00 PM
text: The Federal Reserve is the group that sets the main interest rate. Its meeting runs October 27 and 28, and it shares its decision today at 2:00 PM Eastern time. Interest rates are the price of borrowing money, so they touch almost every stock. Fast growing companies, like many AI names, often move the most when the news is a surprise. We do not know the decision yet.

title: Chip stocks have a big lead
text: AMD closed at $560.26 (up 5.5%), Broadcom at $342.33 (up 4.0%) and TSMC at $436.87 (up 2.9%). AMD sits at 79% of its 52 week range, which is the climb from its lowest to its highest price in the past year. Bigger jumps up can come with bigger drops down. AMD has a beta of 2.45, so it moves a lot more than the market. We could not confirm one single cause for the moves.

title: Rocket Lab swings hard again
text: Rocket Lab closed at $58.31, up 8.3%, but it is still 61% below its 52 week high of $151.00. Its beta is 2.61, the highest on our list, so it is like a roller coaster. Our simple risk score for it is 10 out of 10. A small company that is still growing can rise fast and fall fast.

title: Meta still far from its high
text: Meta closed at $620.19, down 1.6%. It is about 20% below its 52 week high of $779.82. Reports say it fell about 7% on October 22 after its results, as investors weighed how much it plans to spend on AI. Analysts' average price target is $834, which is 35% above today's price, but targets are only guesses and often change.

title: Lesson 26: What is an expense ratio?
text: An expense ratio is the yearly fee a fund charges, shown as a percent of your money. If a fund charges 0.10% and you hold $1,000, you pay about $1 a year. It comes out of the fund automatically, so you never get a bill. Funds like SPY, QQQ and SCHD usually charge low fees, while some funds charge much more. Small fees add up over many years, because that money can no longer grow for you. When you compare two similar funds, the fee is one easy thing to check.

title: What this board covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges, betas and P/E ratios come from FMP. Analyst price targets are available for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, LMT and GE only. Risk scores and the 3, 12 and 36 month scenarios are our own simple estimates, not predictions. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have no target data on the free plan. Prices are from the last close, October 27.
